system_prompt: You are assisting with a factual question about Thai law. State which provision applies and what it requires. Answer in English.
prompt: Somchai borrowed 100,000 baht from Malee with no agreed interest rate, repayable on 1 March 2026. He failed to pay on the due date. If Malee claims default interest for one year, how much is owed? Answer briefly, stating the rate and the amount.
raw_response:
Provision: Civil and Commercial Code (CCC) Section 224 (as amended, B.E. 2564) in conjunction with CCC Section 7. It requires a defaulting debtor on a money debt with no agreed rate to pay default interest at the legal interest rate plus 2% per annum (calculated on principal only). The legal interest rate under Section 7 is 3% p.a., so default interest = 5% p.a.

Rate: 5% per annum
Amount: THB 5,000 default interest for one year (100,000 × 5%); total due THB 105,000.
